newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker with sagging U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker with sagging U.S. market.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker in concert with U.S. bonds, which fell on hedge fund selling, strong economic data and heavy corporate supply, dealers said.
Traders said Canadian bond prices continued to be hit by speculation that interest rate spreads with the U.S. yield curve will widen on possible U.S. interest rate rises.
They said comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday failed to allay fears of a future rise in U.S. interest rates.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.37 to 110.95 to yield 7.075 percent for a spread of 21 basis points.
Participants were glad when Greenspan said on Tuesday that his recent speeches were not meant to move the markets. But the bullish feeling was short-lived.
Last week, Greenspan said that he could not rule out a tightening of monetary policy as a pre-emptive strike against inflationary pressures.
Canada's 10-year bond was down C$0.36 to 103.92 for a yield of 6.449 percent.
